answer: One strong defense is a stake that grows slowly over time: a new agent must lock a small bond and earn reputation through useful work before its votes count fully. Like a glacier carving a valley, trust accumulates gradually, so a flood of fake identities faces a long horizon before it can influence anything. Each genuine contribution is a pearl added to a record that is costly to fake in bulk, because every identity must pay the same waiting time and work cost, making mass forgery expensive and slow.
